repository.workload: Not supplied — a public RealWorld reference implementation with no stated production traffic.

annotation.notes: Retro-annotated from docs/evaluation.md §3.13, an independent blind pass with no memory of this project's own findings and no instruction beyond "review this repository" — the first repository in the evaluation record on the JVM runtime. `forbidden` is intentionally empty: unlike the first batch of ground-truth files, §3.13's write-up documents what the pass correctly reasoned about (SQLite's conceptual-tier confidence cap) only in prose, without a specific file:line for a discarded candidate — encoding one here would mean inventing a location not actually in the source record, which is the exact discipline this corpus exists to hold reviews to. A real, reproducible detector false negative was also found and fixed during this pass (registry.yaml's `sqlite` signal missed the JVM driver coordinate `org.xerial:sqlite-jdbc` and the `jdbc:sqlite:` connection scheme entirely); that is a detect_stack.py regression, already covered by tests/test_detect_stack_regressions.py, not a finding-content question this schema models.

expected.mechanism: Every GraphQL field resolver issues unbatched per-item queries with no DataLoader anywhere in the codebase — an O(N*M) cost under nested queries. The REST path in the same codebase already batches the identical data (ArticleQueryService.setFavoriteCount), which is direct evidence the fix is a known, available pattern rather than new work.

No index on any foreign-key or filter column in the schema (tags.name, article_tags.article_id/tag_id, comments.article_id, follows.user_id/follow_id) — provable directly from the migration file with no runtime evidence needed.

SQLite behind a 10-connection HikariCP pool and a 200-thread Tomcat pool, with no journal-mode or busy-timeout configuration. Confidence is deliberately capped at Medium rather than asserted High or Critical, because SQLite carries no dedicated technology file in this project (registry.yaml notes it as conceptual-tier) and concurrency questions at that tier should be flagged as unknowns rather than asserted with unwarranted certainty — a correct application of graceful degradation, not a missed opportunity.
An unbounded per-tag loop inside a single write transaction on article creation, with no upper bound on the caller-supplied tag list.
